## Purpose and entry points
`prime-rl` is a Python 3.12, NVIDIA-GPU framework for scalable post-training: asynchronous RL, SFT, inference, and evaluation. Console entrypoints under `src/prime_rl/entrypoints/` launch composed TOML configurations: `rl.py` starts the full RL stack; `trainer.py`, `inference.py`, `sft.py`, and `eval.py` run individual services; `orchestrator.py` coordinates externally launched services. Config schemas live in `packages/prime-rl-configs/src/prime_rl/configs/`.

## Configuration and process composition
Configurations define model, algorithm, environment, inference, trainer, orchestration, evaluation, and monitoring settings. The config package is a boundary between CLI/TOML input and runtime-specific objects: `packages/prime-rl-configs/src/prime_rl/configs/rl.py`, `orchestrator.py`, and `trainer.py`. Example and production run definitions are under `configs/` and `examples/`; the `rl` entrypoint composes and supervises inference, orchestration, and training processes.

## Async RL orchestration
The orchestrator implements the central control loop: obtain prompts/environments, dispatch generation work, collect trajectories and rewards/annotations, transform or pack training batches, and send them to training. `src/prime_rl/orchestrator/orchestrator.py` owns lifecycle coordination; `dispatcher.py` and `concurrency.py` control asynchronous throughput; `generation_source.py`, `train_sink.py`, and `trajectories.py` form core stage boundaries. Algorithm implementations select loss/advantage/off-policy behavior, including GRPO, OPD, RAE, and SFT-style paths, in `src/prime_rl/orchestrator/algo/base.py` and `grpo.py`.

## Inference service and model synchronization
Inference is a service boundary used by RL generation and standalone evaluation. It primarily integrates vLLM, including custom server/token serving and routed-expert behavior: `src/prime_rl/inference/server.py`, `src/prime_rl/inference/vllm/server.py`, and `serving_tokens.py`. Trainer updates must reach inference workers through pluggable weight transports—filesystem, NCCL, or NIXL—defined by `src/prime_rl/transports/weights/base.py`, `nccl.py`, and `nixl/nixl.py`. Batch traffic similarly supports filesystem or ZeroMQ in `src/prime_rl/transports/batch/`.

## Training runtime
The trainer consumes SFT datasets or orchestrator-produced RL batches, executes distributed forward/backward/optimization, checkpoints state, and publishes updated weights. RL and SFT paths are separated in `src/prime_rl/trainer/rl/train.py`, `src/prime_rl/trainer/sft/train.py`, and `src/prime_rl/trainer/model.py`. It targets PyTorch/FSDP-style distributed GPU execution with context and expert parallelism, activation/optimizer offload, FP8, LoRA, and MoE runtime support: `src/prime_rl/trainer/parallel_dims.py`, `moe_runtime.py`, and `optim/offload.py`.

## Model implementation boundary
Model selection supports generic Hugging Face causal LMs plus native optimized stacks for large/MoE families. Custom model implementations, conversion, attention, and kernels are grouped beneath `src/prime_rl/trainer/models/`, for example `qwen3_moe/modeling_qwen3_moe.py`, `deepseek_v4/modeling_deepseek_v4.py`, and `glm_moe_dsa/modeling_glm_moe_dsa.py`. This isolates model-family specifics from common trainer and orchestration contracts, while supporting EP/CP and multimodal variants.

## Evaluation, observability, and deployment
Standalone, online, and resumable evaluation flows reside in `src/prime_rl/eval/eval.py`, `online.py`, and `resume.py`; they call inference and can feed results into orchestration. Monitoring is abstracted behind file, Prime, and Weights & Biases implementations: `src/prime_rl/monitors/base.py`, `file/monitor.py`, and `wandb/monitor.py`; the optional dashboard serves local run traces via `src/prime_rl/dashboard/server.py`. Deployment targets local GPUs, Slurm (Jinja launch templates in `src/prime_rl/templates/`), and Kubernetes via `k8s/prime-rl/`. External dependencies include Hugging Face models/datasets, vLLM, NVIDIA NCCL/CUDA, optional Flash Attention, `verifiers` environments, W&B, and Prime Intellect platform services.
